# Didache Chapter 14 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 14 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_014_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 14

**1** On the Lord's Day, come together as a community, break bread, and give thanks. But first — confess your sins. Your sacrifice must be pure.

**2** If you have an unresolved quarrel with another person in the community, don't come to the table until you've made it right. A defiled sacrifice is no sacrifice at all.

**3** This is exactly what the Lord spoke of through the prophet: "In every place and at every time, bring me a pure sacrifice. For I am a great King, says the Lord — and my name is wonderful among the nations."

---

*PNEUMA note: In three verses, the Didache gives us the oldest surviving description of a Christian Sunday service. The structure is: gather, confess, break bread, give thanks. But notice what must happen before anyone comes to the table: confession of sins (v.1) and reconciliation with fellow believers (v.2). The eucharist in this community was not a passive act of receiving — it was a moment of communal moral accountability. The citation of Malachi 1:11 (v.3) is stunning: the Didache community understood themselves to be the fulfillment of Malachi's vision of a universal, pure offering to God from all nations.*
